root_causes.description: Unchanging secret re-read from a remote store (SSM + KMS) on every invocation, with no reuse across warm invocations
No deadline budget across the caller -> verifier -> SSM chain; only the 30 s function timeout bounds waits
Verification implemented as a separate synchronously-invoked function on the blocking path
Unconditional full-payload logging on the hot path
No instrumentation on the verification path
Avoidable module-scope initialization work on cold start

findings.problem: Every valid verification makes a remote ssm.getParameters call with WithDecryption through a newly constructed SSM client to read a value that almost never changes; nothing is reused across warm invocations.
findings.performance_principle: Do not repeat remote work whose result does not change between requests; fixed per-request I/O on a blocking path adds latency to every request and load to a shared dependency.

evidence.statement: getSecret constructs new AWS.SSM() and calls getParameters with WithDecryption: true on each call
getSecret is invoked inside exports.handler, i.e. per invocation; only AWS.config is set at module scope
IAM grants only ssm:GetParameters, consistent with a runtime fetch and no pre-provisioned secret
No runtime evidence (trace, metric, CloudTrail export) was supplied

findings.conditions: Applies at any traffic level as per-request latency; becomes a shared-resource (SSM/KMS throughput) problem only if peak webhook rate is a significant fraction of the account's SSM GetParameters throughput together with other SSM users. Rate is unknown; assumption is bursty low-to-moderate traffic, which keeps severity Medium.

counter_evidence.statement: Searched for module-scope memoization, a parameter-caching extension/layer, or an env-var secret: none found
Searched for a rate cap (API Gateway throttling, reserved concurrency): none in repo
Input-validation early return skips SSM for malformed requests, bounding invalid-traffic load

findings.why_this_might_not_matter: Webhook volume for one GitHub organization may be a handful per minute; one SSM round trip per webhook is then unnoticeable and far from any quota, and warm reuse is not guaranteed for sparse traffic.
findings.recommendation: Construct the SSM client once at module scope and memoize the secret promise per execution environment with a bounded TTL, with a rate-limited refetch on signature mismatch to pick up rotation. Removes the repeated read rather than masking its latency. Hit rate: every warm invocation reuses the single key; invalidation: TTL plus refetch-on-mismatch; granularity: one key; stampede: at most one fetch per concurrently cold environment; consistency: rotation staleness is already inherent and the acceptable window is a product decision.

alternatives.option: Module-scope client + memoized secret with TTL and refetch-on-mismatch
alternatives.why: Removes the call from warm invocations with a few lines, no new infrastructure, secret stays in SSM
Same effect, adds a layer dependency and a local hop
Removes SSM call but ties rotation to redeploys
Defensible only if traffic proves very low

findings.trade_offs: Secret held in memory for the environment's lifetime; staleness window after rotation bounded by TTL; refetch-on-mismatch must be rate-limited so forged requests cannot drive SSM reads.

validation.metric: Ratio of CloudTrail GetParameters events to Lambda Invocations over the same window; warm-invocation Duration p50
validation.expectation: GetParameters calls fall from about one per valid invocation to about one per cold start or TTL expiry; warm Duration falls by the SSM round trip (magnitude unmeasured)
validation.falsifier: GetParameters volume does not drop, meaning environments are not reused at this traffic level and impact was overstated
validation.guard: Unit test asserting getParameters is called once across two handler invocations in one module instance

findings.problem: Neither outbound call on the webhook path (SSM in the verifier, lambda.invoke in the documented caller) has an explicit per-attempt timeout, retry cap, or budget; the only bound in the repo is the 30 s function timeout, during which the synchronous caller is also blocked.
findings.performance_principle: Every remote call on a blocking path needs a bound smaller than its caller's remaining budget; otherwise a slow dependency becomes resource exhaustion in every caller.

evidence.statement: SDK configured with apiVersions and region only; SSM client created with defaults, no httpOptions timeouts or maxRetries
Caller's Lambda client created with defaults and lambda.invoke awaited with no timeout
Function timeout of 30 s is the only time bound
Slots held under SSM degradation ~= 2 x arrival rate x time-to-fail, capped at 30 s per webhook; arrival rate unknown so not sized

findings.conditions: Matters when SSM, KMS, or Lambda invoke is slow or throttling; cost scales with webhook arrival rate. If peak rate x 30 s x 2 approaches unreserved account concurrency (unknown), blast radius becomes system-wide and severity High.

counter_evidence.statement: Searched for client timeouts, SDK retry config, or getRemainingTimeInMillis use: none
The 30 s Lambda timeout bounds the worst case, so this is not an unbounded hang
Searched for reserved concurrency to isolate blast radius: not set

findings.why_this_might_not_matter: SSM is normally fast; at low webhook rates even a 30 s stall holds few slots, and GitHub deliveries can be redelivered.
findings.recommendation: Set explicit connect/read timeouts and a retry cap on both SDK clients, sized so the verifier's total fits inside the caller's remaining time and the caller's inside the gateway's integration timeout. Derive values from measured latency (not yet available); add the bound now and tune from data. PERF-001 also shrinks this exposure to cold starts and TTL refreshes.

alternatives.option: Explicit per-attempt timeout and retry cap on both clients within the caller's budget
alternatives.why: Directly bounds slot hold time; small config change
Blunt; kills slow-healthy calls and does not bound the caller
Isolates blast radius but converts overload to throttles; complementary

findings.trade_offs: Too-short timeouts turn healthy slow calls into 500s and, with retries, add load to SSM during a brownout; values need measurement and revisiting.

findings.problem: The documented pattern has each consumer invoke the verifier with RequestResponse, so the consumer sits idle and billed while a second function runs, cold-starts independently and fetches the secret; the whole event is serialized into the invoke payload and parsed back.
findings.performance_principle: Do not add a synchronous network hop and a second compute unit on a blocking path for work that can be done locally or handed off; each serial hop adds latency, tail and resource hold time.

evidence.statement: new AWS.Lambda() per call; InvocationType RequestResponse; Payload JSON.stringify(event)

No runtime evidence; production consumer usage unknown

findings.conditions: Assumes production consumers follow example.js (unconfirmed). Duration and concurrency cost scale with webhook rate (unknown); cold-start compounding matters when traffic is sparse enough for environments to go cold between deliveries.

counter_evidence.statement: example.js is not deployed by this repo's Terraform (only index.js is zipped), so production use is unproven

findings.why_this_might_not_matter: At low webhook volume the extra billed duration and second concurrency slot are negligible, and secret isolation may be worth more than the cost.
findings.recommendation: Keep isolation but stop blocking the consumer: make the verifier the API Gateway target, verify, then dispatch to downstream functions asynchronously (Event invocation or a queue). If the topology stays, at least construct the Lambda client at module scope in consumers.

alternatives.option: Verifier as front door with async dispatch to consumers

findings.performance_principle: Hot-path instrumentation should be proportional to its diagnostic value; whole-payload logging makes ingestion cost and I/O scale with payload size on every request.

findings.recommendation: Log a bounded summary (delivery id, event type, outcome, duration); gate full-payload logging behind an explicit debug flag; declare the log group with a retention period.
findings.trade_offs: Less raw data for after-the-fact debugging; GitHub's delivery log partly covers it.
